articleTitle: Optimizing PV System Placement in Kirkuk City Power System Using PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Photovoltaics (PV) are a rapidly growing source of energy worldwide and are typically installed as distributed generation in distribution systems. PV technology has emerged as a promising solution for increasing power demand and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Placing PV systems in distribution systems is crucial for overall performance, but it is a complex task with multiple constraints and objectives. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is a metaheuristic optimization technique based on bird flocking behavior that has proven to be a valuable tool for solving optimization problems. The PSO algorithm can find the optimal location, size, and orientation of PV panels in a distribution system, considering power losses, voltage stability, and system capacity. This work analyzes the Kirkuk City Power System (IEEE-5 BusBar) to find the optimal location and size for PV systems, improve voltage levels, and reduce losses. The PSO algorithm compares the power system before and after connecting the PV system.

articleTitle: A Review of Passive Control Flow Past UAV Wings
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: In this paper a number of control surfaces method for UAV performance optimization was objected. An unmanned aerial vehicle is a type of aircraft that operates without any human intervention. Unmanned aerial vehicles are used in many industries and applications, including communications, GIS, border surveillance, research and rescue, scientific and environmental studies, agriculture, as well as the military industries. The advantages of using drones include high efficiency, access to difficult and dangerous zones, cost reduction and human hoarding. However, the use of UAVs also comes with challenges and problems. One of the most important problems is the risk of losing control and running out of fuel and aerodynamic problems at different angles of attack or flow condition around the UAVs that change the performance and stability of UAVs. In this research, the samples are examined, Geometries and shapes changes created on the UAV's wing to improve the aerodynamic coefficients in the low and high angle of attack, flight range and etc. in other words, this current research is to enhance the manoeuvrability of a UAV, performance and stability parameter and aerodynamics behaviour of UAV, a number passive flow control method was employed and studied.

articleTitle: Remotely Controlled Firefighting Robot with ESP32-CAM Module
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Firefighting is one of the most dangerous professions due to its unsafe and constantly changing environment. Firefighters may be required to operate under conditions with an elevated level of uncertainty and must make time-critical decisions using insufficient information. Firefighting robots are specialized robots that are designed to assist with firefighting and rescue operations. These robots can be used to enter hazardous environments that may be too dangerous for human firefighters, such as buildings that are on fire or have collapsed. In this study, we propose a prototype for a remotely controlled firefighting robot that is equipped with a water pump. The robot uses Wi-Fi based ESP32-CAM module that will assist the firefighting and rescue operations by providing a video streaming from the fire environment. This will help the operator to make the correct decisions and movements to perform the firefighting task effectively. In addition, the camera module will provide the operator with updated information on the environmental conditions and will help search for trapped people.

articleTitle: Design of Perfect Absorber based on One-Dimensional Graphene-Silica Metasurface for Infrared radiations
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Graphene is one of the most widely used materials for the implementation of photonic devices due to its excellent advantage of having the ability to tune its optical and electrical properties in a wide range of wavelengths. Here, we proposed a perfect absorber based on a one-dimensional metasurface composed of a three-layer structure of graphene and aluminum oxide which shows a near-perfect absorption of about 98% at the infrared wavelength of λ = 14 μm. Moreover, the proposed perfect absorber shows 95% absorption in a wide-incident angle up to 70 degrees which is one of the best results that have been reported to the best of our knowledge. The results are based on exact simulation done by the method of finite-difference time-domain (FDTD).

articleTitle: Design of High-Performance Optical TE Modulator Based on Si/VO2/Si Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Phase transition in vanadium dioxide (VO2) from insulation to metallic phase, makes it an attractive candidate for the realization of electro-absorption modulators. In this paper, we investigate and design a high-performance modulator at the telecommunication wavelength of λ = 1.55 μm, based on a silicon rib waveguide incorporated with a nanostrip V02 layer. The modulator utilizes an asymmetric structure for enhancing the modulation depth and reaching the minimum insertion loss. We show that for transverse electric optical modes, the asymmetric structure shows better characteristics. The results show a high-modulation depth of about 6.54 dB/μm and the corresponding insertion loss of about 1.34 dB/μm.

articleTitle: Vision Transformer-based Automatic Detection of COVID-19 in Chest X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: The COVID-19 virus, which first emerged in the city of Wuhan in China, rapidly spread across the globe due to its high contagiousness. Detecting the virus early is crucial to stop its spread and to provide timely treatment to affected individuals. Chest X-ray (CXR) images are a quick, cost- effective, and non-invasive method commonly used for the diagnosis of COVID-19. CXR images are manually inspected by experts for diagnosis. However manually detection is not only time-consuming but also prone to errors due to human fatigue. For these reasons, there is an urgent need for a system that can detect COVID-19 from CXR images. In this study, the Vision Transformer (ViT) model was used to classify Normal, Pneumonia, and COVID-19 from CXR images. Experimental results show that the Vision Transformer (ViT) possesses a robust and high generalization capability, with an accuracy rate of 97%, indicating its significant potential in medical image analysis.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effects of Wind Disturbance Speed Behind a Tree Species at a Certain Speed Using a Wind Tunnel
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: When we look at the titles of the journals in the cited literature, we clearly see that the scientific community working on the effects of wind on plants is quite dispersed, from botany to meteorology and forestry to entomology, etc., which has faced various challenges. In this research, we want to experimentally investigate the effect of wind on a type of tree with mechanical science. The wind tunnel is a precise instrument for creating wind with a certain speed, which researchers use in the science of aerospace mechanics, agriculture, etc. (in this research, the wind speed created is 5 meters per second). Analysis of the effect turbulent velocity involves the precise measurement of changes in displacement of the hot wire behind the trees. Investigating the effect of wind disturbance speed behind tree species with a certain speed using a wind tunnel helps us to have a better understanding of the response of trees to the prevailing wind in precise conditions. These results can be used in the correct design of tree support systems in areas with strong winds, improving tree establishment and reducing wind damage.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of K-means and NMF Clustering Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Cluster analysis, also known as clustering, is a multivariate data mining technique whose goal is to classify objects based on a set of selective features. Nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF), and K-means are the most used clustering methods. NMF is a method that breaks down a high-dimensional data matrix into two lower-dimensional matrices with positive elements; while K-means is an algorithm that assigns each data point to a cluster that has a centroid. The main objective of this algorithm is to minimize the total distance between the data points and their respective clusters. In this paper, four datasets, consist of data collected from newswires, radio programs, and television programs are prepared for assessing. Then, they are clustered via NMF and K-means techniques. Furthermore, the results are compared with Purity and Entropy criteria. It can be concluded that both algorithms work better in small dimension datasets rather than high-dimensional ones. Furthermore, NMF has generally a better accuracy.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Simulation of Electric Vehicle Energy Consumption: Incorporating Route Planning and Machine Learning-Based Predictions
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: This study presents an evaluation of predictive models for electric vehicle (EV) energy consumption in a simulated environment. Utilizing a synthetic elevation grid and considering variables such as weather conditions and traffic levels, we implemented the A* algorithm to simulate EV routes and calculate energy costs. The generated dataset was used to train three regression models: Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, and Linear Regression. Model performance was assessed using Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and the R-squared (R2) score. Results indicated that the predictive accuracy of the models was limited, with all models exhibiting low R2 scores and high MSE and MAE values. The study highlights the challenges in predicting EV energy consumption and suggests the need for more complex models or additional features that can better capture the dynamics of energy usage in EVs.

articleTitle: Fox Optimizer and Logistic Regression for Liver Diseases Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Hepatitis C poses a severe threat to public health since it frequently progresses to chronic infections that are fatal without early signs, making prompt detection and diagnosis difficult. To meet this urgent demand, the study quickly suggests a solution: a machine learning model intended for the early diagnosis of liver disorders associated with hepatitis C. Data from the UCI Machine Learning Repository, including patient demographics and internal laboratory values, were thoroughly examined for this investigation. The results highlight machine learning's exciting potential for early illness classification. The test accuracy of the Ensemble Method was a respectable 94%, but it's important to note that Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), and XG-Boost separately outperformed this benchmark with a remarkable 95.7%. Afterward, RF reached an even greater accuracy of roughly 96% using optimizations. In addition, we improved the models' performance by using the FOX Optimizer. Logistic Regression demonstrated an impressive improvement, with 96.7% accuracy and an astounding 99% precision. This significant development demonstrates the power of our machine learning models and the critical role optimization techniques play in pushing the limits of predicted accuracy for better liver disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Universities Cyber Security Standardization
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Standards have been very popular lately in the cyber security field with their power to increase the security maturity and awareness of every company. Having their flexibility to reach different scales starting from small businesses going up to bigger businesses, we did not find the real application of this standards to universities. For that, the mix between several standards like ISO, COBIT and ITIL that have the greatest power over the cyber security work flow, will be a great shift to the digital world that the universities are pursuing.

articleTitle: Optimizing Anthropometric Characteristics Using Two RBF and Kriging Models
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: In this research, using anthropometric parameters (input) and functional characteristics (output) of speed of 5, 10 and 20 meters, the top three male wheelchair tennis players of the Islamic Republic of Iran have been studied. Considering that artificial intelligence and machine learning are very important in the field of optimization and parametric study, our goal is to get the best player with the least cost, time and energy using two machine learning algorithms (kriging) and neural network (RBF) and finally reach the best design (player) using genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: Forensic Handwriting and Signatures Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Given the significance of the messages in these crimes and the signatures in the content of those messages, there is a growing need in the field of forensic analysis to verify these crimes and accusations, as well as to look for evidence in a variety of ways before reaching a final decision regarding the accused individual. In this study, a thorough business model was created as evidence of tremendous relevance, mission, and strong privacy as a fingerprint that separates one individual from another. The suggested model will take into account a number of factors, including the accused's name and the location and date of the incident. To eliminate the need for investigators to guess due to unclear and suspicious handwritten messages containing evidence-either conclusive evidence or evidence that aids in the process of tracking events to reach conclusive evidence-a tool is developed to translate the messages into readable, understandable, and clear content. These resources are designed to help criminal investigators reach the best possible conclusions. The proposed machine was trained using a set of numbers, words, and signatures that had various shapes and patterns. This allowed the system to recognize and validate the signature in all of its forms, including some that were difficult to understand. The proposed model achieved results of more than 98%, compared to the previous studies in this area. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Analysis of Tunable THz Structure Based on Graphene Nano-Material Using Implicit Finite Difference Time Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: In this paper, the analysis of a tunable THz structure based on graphene nano-material with magnetic biasing is presented. In this respect, a periodic magnetized graphene micro-patch array supported by SI0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> glass substrate is analyzed by using an implicit three-stage operator splitting f nite difference time domain (3S-OS-FDTD) method. The presented splitting mechanism decomposes the system's main operator into sub-operators to isolate different characteristics of the graphene layer. The implicit scheme is unconditionally stable, where the temporal discretization is not bounded by the standard Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) stability constraint. Numerical examples are conducted and it is observed that the transmission coeff cient of the presented graphene structure can be tuned by changing the chemical potential of the graphene and the magnetic biasing intensity, and this makes the graphene to be a good candidate in future THz communication systems and tunable devices design.

Author Keywords: implicit f nite difference time domain

articleTitle: Red Palm Weevil Treatment Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Annually, palm trees face a threat from palm AIDS, a condition caused by the infiltration of the red palm weevil into the tree trunk. This pest silently gnaws away at the palm tree without clear early symptoms. Symptoms typically manifest when it's too late to save the tree. To address this issue, we have developed a robot equipped with sensors including sound, radiological imaging, and soil moisture and acidity sensors that promptly detect signs of infestation. This robot employs two arms to administer therapeutic treatments upon receiving signals from the interconnected sensor circuit. Our experiments have successfully demonstrated the robot's ability to respond effectively to the presence of the insect as indicated by sensor signals.

articleTitle: Speed Control of BLDC Motor: Design and Simulation Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Traditional speed control methods for BLDC motors often rely on conventional control algorithms, which may have limitations in terms of accuracy and adaptability. The neural network is designed to learn the nonlinear characteristics of the BLDC motor and adaptively adjust the control signals to achieve precise speed control. The neural network architecture is carefully constructed to capture the complex relationships between the motor inputs and outputs. The simulation environment is established using MatLab/SIMULINK, and the proposed neural network-based speed control system is implemented and tested. System performance is evaluated under various operating conditions, including different speed references. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed neural network-based speed control system. The system exhibits superior performance in terms of accuracy, robustness, and adaptability compared to traditional control methods. It successfully maintains the desired speed in the presence of disturbances and load variations, showcasing the neural network's ability to learn and adapt. The results of this study expand BLDC motor control methods and may spur other advancements in the area of neural network-based control systems.

articleTitle: DE-ColonSegNet: An Improved version of ColonSegNet with dual encoder for accurate real-time Polyp segmentation in colonoscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: High-performance real-time automatic polyp detection is crucial to gastrointestinal healthcare. Efficient detection systems can aid in early diagnosis and intervention, significantly impacting patient outcomes. This study aims to develop an algorithm that strikes a superior balance between computational performance and accuracy compared to existing solutions. Achieving this balance is essential for practical, real-time implementation in clinical settings. The DE-ColonSegNet model architecture is presented as the approach to address the computational performance/accuracy trade-off. This model has been designed to optimize detection accuracy and efficiency, utilizing advanced techniques in deep learning. The DE-ColonSegNet model demonstrates promising outcomes, with an average precision of 0.8845, a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.7637, and a dice coefficient of 0.8470. These results showcase the model's effectiveness in accurately identifying and segmenting polyps. The robust performance metrics suggest its potential for practical application in real-time clinical settings, contributing to enhanced efficiency in gastrointestinal healthcare.

articleTitle: Towards Advancing Distributed Data Mining: Intelligent Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Distributed data mining (DDM) deals with the analysis of distributed data and proposes algorithmic solutions to perform different data analysis and mining operations in a distributed manner by considering resource constraints. Here, patterns are discovered, and predictions are implemented based on multiple distributed data sources. However, DDM faces several problems in terms of performance and implementation. Specifically, the main problems include issues of autonomy and privacy, which this paper aims to solve. The distributed sites must be in the same environment or organization and under the control of the same administration, implying their agreement on the same classification algorithm. Consequently, the best solution is the use of intelligent agent systems that contain a group of autonomous agents with communication and coordination facilities with different classification algorithms and environments, can collaborate with each other, and can decide whether and when to request information from other agents.

articleTitle: Improving Image Captioning Using Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Image captioning is a challenging task that requires a computer vision system to generate natural language descriptions for images. The aim is to build a model that can comprehend the visual content of an image and produce a coherent and accurate caption for it. This technology has various applications in domains such as assistive technology for visually impaired people, image search engines, image understanding in artificial intelligence systems, education, social media, and more. In recent years, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with long-short-term memory (LSTM) units have been widely used for image captioning. However, RNNs have some limitations in capturing long-term dependencies and modeling complex language structures. In this paper, we propose a novel image captioning method that uses a convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract image features and a bidirectional encoder representation of transformers (BERT) to generate captions. BERT is an advanced language model that uses a transformer architecture to learn bidirectional context embeddings for words in a sentence. We train our hybrid model on a small-scale dataset of images and captions. We evaluate our model on several metrics and compare it with LSTM method. Our results show that our model achieves reliable performance and acceptable error rate (loss score). We also demonstrate that our model can generate more diverse and rich captions than RNN-based models.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Data Dynamics Based on Wavelet Coherence Using Higher-Order Moments
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: The article addresses the challenges of analyzing data represented as time series, depicting the evolution of a specific process, phenomenon, or object over time. Special emphasis is placed on conducting a comparative analysis of the dynamics among different data sets; so, to achieve this, a method for estimating wavelet coherence is employed. The approach includes transforming the original data through a sliding sampling window using higher-order moments to capture the memory effect. This methodology enables the assessment of dynamics in extensive data sets, thereby enhancing the efficiency of processing and analysis. The article presents results based on real data, providing an additional evaluation of their mutual dynamics. The findings affirm the reliability and effectiveness of such an analysis.

articleTitle: A Fractional Study for Solving the Smoking Model and the Chaotic Engineering Model
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: In this study, a novel scheme for the Caputo-Fabrizio fractional derivative (CFFD) is employed to solve the fractional smoking model and a chaotic electrical model. Illustrations comparing the results between the proposed method and RK4 have been presented. It has been discovered that the proposed method yields solutions equivalent to the approximate solutions produced by the other methods. Therefore, the strategy can be generalized to other systems to obtain more precise results. The use of this Caputo-Fabrizio fractional derivative scheme has remarkable potential in engineering disciplines. Its ability to detect chaos in diverse systems-like weather patterns, mechanical vibrations, and financial markets-promises a revolutionary approach to managing complex, nonlinear dynamics. Additionally, its equivalence to established techniques, such as RK4, in control systems and signal processing offers avenues for more accurate modeling and control, enhancing system stability. In biomedical engineering, its adaptability to disease modeling could lead to significant advancements in predicting and managing various health conditions. This scheme's demonstrated reliability and versatility across different systems suggest its potential as a go-to tool for solving intricate challenges in engineering and science in the future.

articleTitle: Greedy Overall-Relevancy (GOR): An Efficient Greedy Search for Feature Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Various feature selection strategies such as brute-force search, randomized and sequential search have been suggested to remove the redundant features, among which, sequential search strategy is computationally efficient. In this paper, an efficient sequential feature selection method based on greedy search and gain ratio criterion is proposed to select the most informative features from a feature set. The proposed method called greedy overall-relevancy (GOR) which overcomes the blemishes of forward and backward sequential search as commonplace greedy methods. To examine the goodness of selected features, nearest neighbor (NN), Naïve Bayes and edited KNN classifiers were employed. Ten well-known datasets from the standard UCI repository data sets are used to assess the performance of the proposed algorithm in comparison with other state-of-the-art sequential methods. Applying the proposed feature selection and the modified NN to the UCI datasets enhanced the classification accuracy remarkably compare to the other employed methods.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Decision Trees, Random Forest, and k-Nearest Neighbors in Predictive Analytics for Orange Telecom's Customer Complaint Data
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: The study examines the application of machine learning algorithms, namely Decision Trees, Random Forest, and k-Nearest Neighbors, for improving predictive analytics in customer complaint management at Orange Telecom. An analysis is conducted to evaluate the accuracy, efficiency, and scalability of these algorithms in this specific context. Emphasis is placed on thorough data preparation and algorithm assessment, using established performance metrics. Findings provide valuable insights into the handling of complex customer data by these algorithms, underscoring the importance of detailed data preparation for predictive analysis in the telecommunications sector.

articleTitle: Predicting Customer Behavior Using Neural Network Optimized by Grasshopper Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Digital marketing, as an essential branch of science, could provide value for commercial organizations and strengthen the interaction with customers via increasing the electronic services. In digital marketing, real-time analysis of customer behaviors is considered as a key program, which could encourage novel advertisement concentration. Each deal that is assigned to a costumer, is a part of individual behavior and is a sample of feature vectors based on a set of interactions is modelled for creating the customer behavior. In this research, using data mining techniques and metaheuristic algorithms, the patterns of customer behavior are identified and predicted. Neural network as a classifier with acceptable performance is used for complex tasks. In the train phase, neural network is usually worked with back propagation algorithm. This algorithm suffers from falling into the local optima and needs to adjust the weights and using proper initialization weights. To optimize both weights and structure of the neural network, we adopt grasshopper evolutionary algorithm to adjust the weight in an iterative manner along with the adjusting the number of neurons in the hidden layer. In the proposed method, the probability of falling in the local optima is reduced and also the suggested algorithm could provide acceptable performance compared to the other rivals in a rich benchmark of digital marketing.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection with Ensemble of Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Brain tumors are recognized as one of the most lethal cancer types worldwide. Detecting brain tumors using medical imaging techniques is a challenging task due to their complex anatomical structures. Traditional methods rely on specialists meticulously examining MRI scan images. However, this approach is not only time-consuming but also carries a significant risk of error. Therefore, there is a need for more effective methods to detect brain tumors from MRI images. In this study, an ensemble model was proposed for classifying tumor types using MRI scans. Initially, sixteen well-known Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models and four Vision Transformer (ViT) models were trained on the Brain Tumor Dataset, which contains 3264 MRI scan images. Subsequently, by combining the top three high-performing models, we achieved a robust classification performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed model provides a satisfactory performance comparedto existing methods.

articleTitle: Developing a Non-Invasive Eye Tracking Screening Tool for early Detection of Alzheimer's Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a common neurodegenerative condition that impairs daily functioning, memory, and cognition. The ability to treat and manage the disease effectively depends on early detection, but current diagnostic techniques frequently fall short of this goal. This study assesses the potential of eye tracking parameters, remarkably smooth pursuit amplitude, and fixation stability, as biomarkers for AD screening in the early-mid stages to address this issue. A visual tracking task is used in the study to measure participants' fixation stability and smooth pursuit amplitude. The sample includes individuals diagnosed with AD and healthy older adults, to compare eye-tracking parameters between the two groups. The study's findings show that smooth pursuit amplitude and fixation stability are significantly different between AD and healthy controls. This study highlights the importance of investigating novel and non-invasive methods for early detection of AD and establishes the foundation for further investigations in this area. The results of this study will help develop a cost-effective screening tool that is easily accessible for early-stage AD. Importantly, the study reported that the AUC of the AD group was 0.966 and the AUC of the control group was 0.869, with a sensitivity of 93% and specificity of 100%, and an overall accuracy of 96.5%. The promising findings of this study will help create a low-cost screening tool that is easily accessible for AD in its early stages.

articleTitle: The Significance of Utilizing the dependencies among Labels in Multi Label Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Multi-Label Classification (MLC) is a general type of classification that attracted scholars in the last few years. It imposes a high challenge since the problem search space of MLC is very large and follows an exponential function of growth. Moreover, the accuracy of classification in MLC is still very low when compared to the accuracy of Single Label Classification (SLC). Consequently, many scholars and researchers proposed to utilize and exploit the dependencies among class labels in to minimize the size of the problem search space of MLC, and hence, improve the accuracy of the classification task. Unfortunately, very few studies address this issue and attempt to discover the benefits of utilizing and exploiting the dependencies among labels in the domain of MLC. Therefore, this research attempts to identify the significance of discovering and utilizing these dependencies, with respect to three evaluation metrics designed specifically for MLC, and considering four different multi label datasets. The results revealed the clear significance of discovering and utilizing high order dependencies among labels in MLC, especially with high cardinality datasets.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of Temperature Variations on the Performance of Thermoelectric Generators
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Recent advancements in renewable energy technologies have brought Thermoelectric Generators (TEGs) to the forefront, primarily due to their ability to efficiently convert waste thermal energy into electrical power across multiple power levels. This study delves into the environmental benefits and operational efficiencies of TEGs, highlighting their zero-emission, silent operation, and low maintenance requirements. A significant portion of this research is dedicated to exploring the influence of temperature differential (ΔT) on the efficacy of TEGs, as temperature is a crucial factor in the energy conversion process. The electrical representation of TEGs is modeled as a voltage source in series with an internal resistance, while its thermal aspect comprises parallel-connected p- and n-type thermocouples. The study aims to meticulously analyze the behavior of TEG models under various thermal gradients and to scrutinize their electrical characteristics under different load conditions. This is achieved through comprehensive experimental methodologies, with the findings underscoring the impact of temperature variations on both hot and cold sides of TEGs on all electrical parameters. It is observed that an increase in the temperature difference results in a corresponding rise in both the maximum power output and the open-circuit voltage. In essence, the efficiency of TEGs is noted to improve with a higher and more stable temperature differential.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Power of Gamma Rays in Material Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Unlocking the Power of Gamma Rays in Material Analysis. Mate-rial characterization plays a pivotal role in both industrial and medical sec-tors, relying on radiation as a fundamental tool. In this investigation, we ex-plored the characterization of various liquid solutions, each characterized by distinct densities, employing an Am-241 gamma emitter source. Our study delved into the influence of material density on both transmitted and scat-tered gamma ray intensities, while also shedding light on the impact of gam-ma ray scattering angles on scattered ray intensity. Intriguingly, our findings revealed a consistent trend: an increase in material density corresponded to a decrease in transmitted gamma ray intensity, with notable exceptions. These exceptions were attributed to the presence of covalent bonds within certain solutions, which significantly influenced radiation interactions with the material. This discovery underscores the importance of recognizing that material characterization goes beyond density considerations alone. Factors such as atomic number and chemical structure should also be factored into the equation when employing specific radiation sources for specialized material analyses.

Author Keywords: European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer

articleTitle: Automated Solar Panel Cleaning System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Solar panels have a significant impact on our world by providing an environmentally friendly alternative to traditional power generation plants that can harm the environment. However, it is crucial to recognize that solar power plants require regular cleaning. When solar panels are not cleaned regularly, environmental dust accumulates on their surfaces and transforms into a sticky layer due to morning dew. This dust accumulation leads to a decrease in the efficiency of the solar panel. In our research, we have developed an automated cleaning system for solar panels. This system eliminates the need for manual cleaning efforts and ensures that solar panels remain clean and efficient. This system reduces human efforts, which saves time, and works automatically, resulting in increasing the efficiency of the solar panel. The cleaning is achieved using a water-based Roller brush. Two ac motors with inverters are used for the brush and the system's assembly motions. A control unit based on Arduino is built to perform the cleaning task with the aid of limit switches, relays, electric valves, and other electrical and electronic tools. The brush is attached to the movable assembly of the system. This brush remains in contact with the panel. When the assembly of the system moves, water flows through sprinkles on panels and brush move on the surface of the panel and removes the dust. The proposed system is tested and evaluated by comparing the electrical parameters (maximum power, voltage, and current) for the solar panel before and after cleaning. Results show that the efficiency is increased when the solar panel is regularly cleaned.

articleTitle: Comparison Between Rectangular and Circular Microstrip Patch Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: In this paper, several designs of microstrip array antennas suitable for wireless communication applications are presented. This paper demonstrates several shapes of microstrip array antennas, such as rectangular and circular patch antenna arrays. Specifically, single, 2 × 1, and 4 × 1 elements of both shapes are designed and simulated by High Frequency Structural Simulator (HFSS). Moreover, this paper presents a comparison between both rectangular and triangular antenna arrays. Since the resonance frequency of these antennas is 2.4 GHz, these antennas are suitable for the ISM band and WLAN).

articleTitle: Analysis and Development of the Kofr Al-Labad Well Solar Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Renewable energy technologies are becoming increasingly competitive with traditional energy technologies, due to their continually improving performance, low cost, and growing recognition of their environmental and economic benefits. Solar energy harnessing systems offer the advantage of emitting no pollutants into the atmosphere, unlike the combustion of fossil fuels. This project aims to study the design of the network connected to the photovoltaic system of the Kafr El-Labad Cooperative Society, by working with more than one scenario to achieve the best production and cost design. The capacity of the pump is approximately 120 horsepower, in addition to the presence of a few lighting loads. The project will analyze and develop the solar power plant from a technical and economic point of view, and present proposals and recommendations to raise the efficiency of the system.

articleTitle: Harmonic Analysis in the Arab American University Power System: Reasons, Nature, and Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: This study investigates harmonic distortions in the Arab American University (AAUP) grid, which receives electricity from Tubas District Electricity Company (TDECO) through 11 transformers. The project collected data using power quality analyzers on four transformers, focusing on two key indicators: total harmonic distortion and total demand distortion. Results indicate that total demand distortion is a more reliable indicator and, so far, all transformers remain within IEEE limits. Future work aims to expand the analysis seasonally and encourages others to assess remaining transformers.

articleTitle: Human-Computer Interaction in Augmented Reality: Applications and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: a technique called Augmented Reality (AR) superimposes digital data on the physical world. This technology has the power to completely change how humans communicate with computers. Nonetheless, a number of issues still need to be resolved before AR user interfaces can be made to feel intuitive, natural, and effective. The applications and prospects of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) in AR are covered in this paper. Compared to conventional user interfaces, the authors contend that AR has the potential to produce more engaging and natural user interfaces. They also make the point that in order to fully grasp this potential, AR designers must create new interaction strategies and design tenets.

articleTitle: Energy-Saving Gypsum Bricks with Recycled Stone Powder for Sustainable Buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: This research highlights the importance of creating gypsum bricks that are environmentally sustainable, have excellent thermal and water insulation properties, and contribute to significant energy savings. The process involves using stone powder waste (SW) to produce the bricks. The goal is to replace SW content with three different percentages (5%, 10%, and 15%) to create energy-saving gypsum bricks and compare them with a reference sample of 100% gypsum. Several physical and mechanical tests, including viscosity, compressive strength, setting time, water absorption, and density assessments, are conducted to examine the materials thoroughly. The results show that incorporating recycled SW into brick production offers substantial benefits, particularly in conserving energy within buildings. Therefore, creating gypsum bricks that are environmentally sustainable, have superior specifications, and use SW represents a pivotal initiative in promoting a sustainable society. This also opens the door to deeper considerations regarding their widespread integration into the construction industry, ultimately contributing to substantial energy savings.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Epileptic Seizures in TLE Patients by Improved Cepstrum Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Epilepsy is a common chronic brain disease characterized by recurrent seizures. The most effective way to detection the arrival of an epileptic seizure is EEG analysis. Various methods have been proposed in the detection of epilepsy. The article proposes the combination of the AutoRegressive and Cepstrum methods, taking into account the periodic characteristics of the amplitude and frequency of epileptic seizures compared to seizure-free periods in brain signals. Once the signal is received and pre-processed, the AR model of the signal is calculated and the Cepstrum is obtained on the modeled signal, then the Cepstrum coefficients are averaged within the given interval, and a detection of epileptic seizure is made by thresholding the averaged coefficients. TLE patients were selected in this study due to their higher prevalence compared to other types of epilepsy. The proposed detection algorithm was examined on 11 EEG patients with temporal lobe epilepsy. The results indicate that the proposed method has an accuracy of 98.3% and a false positive rate of 0.5%, which demonstrates its superiority over existing methods, especially considering the presence of various artifacts in the available data. Moreover, owing to its low computational complexity, the proposed method can be integrated into real-time implant detection systems.

articleTitle: Greenhouse Automation using ESP32: A Comprehensive Study on Monitoring and Controlling Environmental Parameters for Optimal Plant Growth
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Greenhouse automation using ESP32 is a novel approach to achieving optimal plant growth by monitoring and controlling environmental parameters. This study presents the design, development, and implementation of an ESP32-based greenhouse monitoring and control system. The system includes sensors for temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and light intensity, enabling real-time data collection from the greenhouse. The ESP32 then processes and analyzes the data and controls the environmental parameters accordingly. This ESP32-based system offers better accuracy and reliability compared to conventional greenhouse monitoring systems. It can potentially improve crop yield and quality significantly and thus is an essential step towards sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: GWSVM: A Robust GMM-Based Pattern Weighting for SVM
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Support Vector Machine (SVM) is an efficient classifier due to its generalization capability; however, it suffers from high sensitivity to noisy data. A new weighted SVM classifier is proposed here to overcome this problem by a pattern weighting approach based on Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM), called hereinafter GWSVM. The weight learning is a procedure of knowledge extraction from the feature space. First, a clustering phase is carried out according to Gap Statistic and Subtractive Clustering (SC) methods. Then a GMM is trained using the clustered data and pattern weights are determined based on the GMM outputs. In the third phase, a redefined optimization formula regarding the weighted patterns is used, so SVM decision boundary is adjusted sensibly. GWSVM is applied to some UCI repository datasets and its performance is presented. The results show the supremacy of our novel classifier in comparison with other versions of SVM. Further, to evaluate robustness and generalization power of GWSVM, the impact of white noise with different variances is investigated. Applying GWSVM and SVM classifiers to noisy data manifests effectiveness of GWSVM in noisy environment.

articleTitle: Study and Analysis of The Kafr Rai Electricity Network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: The importance of electricity in our daily lives cannot be overstated, and it has become an essential necessity. Continuous monitoring and analysis of electrical networks are crucial to stay abreast of network conditions, accommodate growing electrical demands, and prevent network issues that could lead to damage and power disruptions for consumers. In this project, we employ the ETAP program to study and analyze the electrical network in Kafr Rai, located in the West Bank of Palestine. Our objective is to identify network problems contributing to electrical losses and decreased reliability. Subsequently, we propose and implement solutions within the ETAP program to enhance network reliability and prevent potential penalties from the electrical supply company.

articleTitle: Automated Classifications for Stress Symptoms investigations and Stress Prediction Using Machine Learning Based Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Stress is a prevalent illness that leads to mental and physical distress. Machine learning models can assist in stress management by analyzing individual data and providing tailored solutions. They detect stressors, suggest relaxing methods, and offer coping solutions, improving mental health and resilience by tracking trends and providing feedback. The use of machine learning enables automated symptom classification and stress level prediction. Therefore, this research aims to develop a model for predicting cardiovascular disease using relevant characteristics. The investigation used a stress prediction benchmark dataset from Kaggle with seven distinct stress-related parameters. Model development utilized algorithms such as k-nearest neighbors, Naïve Bayes, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and Support Vector Machine. The research also attempted to identify correlations between the dataset's attributes using standard techniques and employ these correlations for stress prediction. Decision Tree provides more accurate predictions in less time, making it useful for medical professionals as a decision-support mechanism.

articleTitle: Contrast as a Method of Image Processing in Increasing Diagnostic Efficiency When Studying Liver Fatty Tissue Levels
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: The paper addresses several challenges associated with analyzing digital medical images, focusing on identifying and assessing fatty liver tissue levels. The methodology enhances the perception of transition zones delineating fatty lesions by employing a contrast technique on the input image. Classic histogram equalization is utilized for contrast, ensuring an even distribution of brightness levels. The evaluation of processed image quality relies on indicators such as entropy, NIQE, and BRISQUE. The paper explores diverse strategies for enhancing the original image based on individual or combined values of quality indicators, which effectively improves the identification of transition zones in fatty lesions. The findings are illustrated using real digital images of fatty liver lesions.

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy Consumption of Residential Buildings Using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: In this study, the amount of energy cost savings for a period of ten years has been calculated using the P_1-P_2 method, which is one of the economical methods of energy life cycle insulation analysis. This method is one of the most popular and practical methods available to calculate the cost of energy savings as well as the thickness of thermal insulation for long periods of time. In this research, genetic algorithm method has been used for optimization. In a genetic algorithm, each optimization variable is a gene, and the combination of all the optimization variables together forms a chromosome. Finally, the results of energy saving for the optimal insulation thickness over a period of ten years using the P_1-P_2 method for the four heating and cooling systems for insulation only and insulation mode considering the reduction of system size in Tehran using The method of optimizing the genetic algorithm is investigated. Author Keywords: insulation thickness calculation and energy saving

articleTitle: Arabic Calligraphy Generation Through Image-to-Image Translation Using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Arabic calligraphy is a revered art form in the Arab world that has seen limited exploration in automated generation due to its complex nature and aesthetic principles and rules. However, recent advancements in deep learning provide promising avenues to address this challenge. In this work, we investigate the automatic generation of Arabic Calligraphy through image-to-image translation. Our approach utilizes Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), a highly effective class of deep learning models recognized for their exceptional data generation abilities, to convert source font images (such as Arial) into desired calligraphy styles. Additionally, we propose a dataset comprising aligned images of conventional font and corresponding calligraphy styles. We evaluate the quality of the generated images on the proposed dataset. Our experiments yield promising results, demonstrating significant progress in the automatic generation of Arabic calligraphy images.

articleTitle: Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler Data Analytics Using a Hybrid of Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: This article presents a hybrid of machine learning techniques for predicting and analyzing Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler (ADCP) data. ADCP is a commonly used instrument for measuring ocean, river, and lake water currents. However, the data generated by ADCP instruments makes it challenging to analyze and extract valuable insights. The study uses three datasets with 25 features, including horizontal velocity components essential for environmental monitoring and management. In this study, we propose a hybrid of machine learning approaches that combines the strengths of multiple algorithms, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Logistic Regression, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and Fuzzy c-Means (FCM). Firstly, we predict ADCP data and analyze its accuracy compared to conventional prediction methods. Secondly, we used P-value and correlation analyses to perform sensitivity analysis to identify the patterns of ADCP data based on the proof of concept discovered by the domain experts. The results show that the CNN model provides better accuracy than the results before features extraction. Furthermore, the sensitivity analysis helps identify the presence of horizontal velocity components deemed crucial by domain experts. Overall, this study highlights the potential of machine learning and data analytics techniques for improving ADCP data analysis and prediction in various water monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Optimum-Location of PV in Distribution System using NR Method with Matlab-ETap Program
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: This paper presents a method for optimizing photovoltaic (PV) system placement in distribution systems using the Newton-Raphson (NR) method with MATLAB code and E-Tap program load flow analysis. The proposed approach utilizes MATLAB code to calculate the optimal location and size of PV systems for maximum Voltage Level and minimum power losses. E-Tap program load flow analysis is used to simulate the distribution system and to validate the results obtained from the MATLAB code. The study provides a detailed explanation of the methodology used for the optimization and validation process. The Newton-Raphson method begins with an initial estimate of the root, denoted x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>≠xr, and uses the tangent of f(x) at x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> to improve on the estimate of the root. The expected outcomes include reduced power losses and improved Voltage Levels. The paper concludes with simulation results and a discussion of the potential benefits of the proposed approach. Also, we are working on analyses of the Kirkuk Power System (IEEE-5 Bus Bar). Find the Optimum Location and Size for the PV system in Kirkuk Power System (IEEE-5 BB). We use a PV system to improve the Voltage Level and reduce Losses in the Kirkuk Power System (IEEE-5 BB). Compare the power system before and after connecting the PV system using E-TAP and MATLAB software.

articleTitle: Simulating of Magnetoencephalography Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Neural brain activities can be non-invasively characterized by analyzing both magneto encephalogram (MEG) and electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. Since the content of MEGs is more informative than EEGs, in this study, modeling of MEG signals is investigated to understand how MEGs are produced. To construct the right magnetic field, the location of magnetic dipoles inside the brain should be determined. In this way, a valid dataset of MEGs belong to different subjects was employed and by applying the inverse method to the MEGs, the location dipoles were detected and then by applying a forward model to the estimated dipoles and using a realistic head model, the simulated MEGs are produced. To see how the simulated signals are similar to the real ones, their power spectrum in different bands and their complexity (Lyapunov exponent) are compared. The comparison results demonstrate enough accuracy between the simulated and the real MEGs in all channels belong to different subjects.

articleTitle: Utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks and KMeans Clustering for Efficient Plant Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: The agricultural sector is pivotal to many economies, but its productivity is frequently hampered by various plant diseases, especially those affecting leaves. Timely and precise detection of these diseases is vital for preserving field health. While image segmentation, clustering, and deep learning are prevalent techniques, our study presents a novel hybrid method for image classification. This strategy integrates the k-means clustering algorithm with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Initially, k-means pinpoints the diseased portions of a leaf, which is followed by the CNN determining the exact disease. For validation, the PlantVillage dataset was employed, which includes various crops facing diverse disease challenges. The determination of the optimal k-value was assessed using the Silhouette coefficient, Elbow method, and Kneedle Algorithm. The Kneedle Algorithm emerged as the most consistent in selecting the optimal k-value. Images were then segmented using k-means clustering based on the k value derived from the Kneedle Algorithm. A CNN was subsequently trained to classify the type of disease from these segmented leaf images, achieving high accuracy and highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Underwater Images Enhancement Based on Gray-Wolf Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Due to the expansion of underwater discoveries and the prevalence of waterproof cameras, underwater imaging and monitoring is expanding day by day. Due to the noise of the underwater environment, the images obtained from underwater have low quality and a lot of noise. In this article, we have proposed an adaptive brightness correction method that adjusts the enhancement performance parameters according to the characteristics of the distribution of the image brightness components and by using the gray wolf algorithm to minimize the error function caused by the mean squared error (MSE) criterion. We want to improve the quality of the image. Optimization is done using alpha, beta and gamma wolves. A wolf is assumed to be the main alpha leader of the algorithm, and beta and delta wolves also participate, and the rest of the wolves are considered as their followers. The proposed model has a satisfactory output compared to different strategies. In addition, simultaneously improving the contrast and improving the color of the image makes the method have a combined capability.

articleTitle: Close Loop Speed Control of DC Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: DC motors are widely used in various industrial, commercial, and residential applications due to their simplicity, reliability, and versatility. However, to achieve precise control over the speed, direction, and torque of a DC motor, a closed-loop control system is often required. In this project, we explore the design, implementation, and evaluation of a closed-loop control system for a DC motor, using a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller. The project consists of several stages, including system modeling and simulation, hardware implementation, user interface design, and performance evaluation. The simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the closed-loop control system can achieve accurate and stable motor control, with fast response time and minimal overshoot. The system can also be easily customized and expanded to suit different motor specifications and control requirements. This study contributes to the advancement of DC motor control technology and opens new opportunities for practical applications in various fields.

articleTitle: Automated Submission of Digital Content to Digital Repositories Through Web API
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Digital repositories are an important tool for the preservation of academic resources in digital format. Submission of items to digital repositories is mainly performed through Web forms which are filled and submitted by human archivist. Submitting a large number of items through Web forms proves to be highly unpractical and time consuming since items should be submitted one item at a time. To address this problem, an approach to automate the submission process of digital resources to digital repositories is proposed. In this approach, metadata about the items stored in spreadsheets are mapped to objects representing digital repository constructs, which are then automatically submitted to a digital repository by means of Web API. The benefits include the simplification of the submission process, the conservation of business resources, and the elimination of redundancy in business operations.

articleTitle: Bitcoin Price Prediction Using Cuckoo Search Algorithm for Feature Selection with LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Deep learning is now a top method for predicting the price of Bitcoin, providing an excellent and well thought out strategy. This technique makes use of a wealth of historical data from reliable sources covering the first ten years of Bitcoin. Technical data and complex patterns are deeply integrated into the dataset to enhance the model's comprehension of complex Bitcoin price patterns. These additions greatly deepen our understanding of the various factors affecting the price of Bitcoin. This method is based on a strategic procedure that involves the careful selection of certain high-performing characteristics. These traits go through a stringent screening process that uses advanced algorithms such as the Cuckoo algorithm. The chosen features are then smoothly incorporated into an encoder-decoder model of LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory), improving the model's ability to predict Bitcoin prices. In this case, it is critical to apply deep learning methods, especially the LSTM encoder-decoder model. Through the integration of technical indicators and sophisticated selection techniques with historical Bitcoin data, this approach leverages deep learning capabilities to identify intricate patterns in Bitcoin pricing movements. In the end, this gives the model the ability to forecast future changes in the price of Bitcoin with accuracy.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Detection of Defect-Free Bangles: Machine Vision Approach for Quality Assurance in Bangle Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: This study explores the application of deep learning and machine vision methods to identify defect-free, circular bangles. The main objective is to improve quality control in the manufacturing of bangles. The study introduces a new model that achieves a remarkable mean Average Precision (mAP) score of 99.1%, showcasing its exceptional accuracy and efficiency in the identification and categorization of bangles. The model successfully differentiates between “good,” “defect,” and “broken” bangles, as evidenced by thorough testing and analysis. During the testing phase, the model regularly achieved a 99% average detection rate for recognizing “good” bangles, hence confirming its capacity to properly detect perfect bangles. Moreover, the model demonstrated remarkable competence in detecting “defect” bangles, achieving detection rates ranging from 98% to 97%, thereby emphasizing its efficacy in recognizing flawed goods. During the analysis phase, the model consistently and precisely recognized “defect” and “broken” bangles, achieving an average detection rate of 98%. This confirms its capability to effectively classify various types of bangles. The model's high mean average precision (mAP) value, along with its exceptional testing and analysis results, highlights its promise as a reliable and effective solution for quality control in bangle manufacturing applications. This study highlights the substantial advantages of utilizing machine vision and deep learning for accurate quality assurance in bangle manufacturing.

articleTitle: PSO Optimized Nonlinear Control of DC Microgrid with Intelligent Energy Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: To meet the United Nations climate stabilization goals by 2050, Clean Energy is playing a vital role to minimize global warming. This study proposes a Clean Energy DC Microgrid with a 2-level control structure. A high level controller consisting of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based Energy Management System (EMS) with maximum power point tracking (MPPT) schemes and a local level Quick Reaching Law based Global Terminal Sliding Mode Controller (QRL-GTSMC). The Microgrid consists of a Fuel Cell (FC), Electrolyzer, Hydrogen Tank, Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), Photovoltaic (PV) array and a Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS). The inclusion of multiple Distributed Energy Resources (DER) increases the complexity of the system but also provides more flexibility. The proposed configuration provides a Hydrogen cycle with production, storage and utilization. The ANN EMS is trained by data accumulated through a State Logic Controller (SLC). The local level control laws are synthesized using QRL-GTSMC, and the resultant parametric variables are tuned by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm using Integral of Absolute Error (IAE) as the minimization performance index. The system's overall stability, response and performance is tested by introducing uncertainties in the form of changing weather conditions. The results are compared with conventional control technique without a reaching law. The proposed system has been evaluated using the MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Comparing Tunnel Junctions for Improved Efficiency of InGaP/GaAs Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: This study aims to enhance the efficiency of InGaP/GaAs solar cells by comparing three different types of tunnel junctions. The objective is to achieve greater efficiency than with InGaP/GaAs or GaAs/GaAs tunnel junction solar cells. To attain this goal, the TCAD Atlas program was used to adjust the thickness and concentration of the tunnel junction. The simulation results revealed that InGaP/InGaP had the highest power conversion efficiency of 42.98%, followed closely by InGaP/GaAs with 42.77%, and GaAs/GaAs with 41.10%. All three types showed high fill factors and external quantum efficiency. The study concludes by comparing the results of the InGaP/InGaP tunnel junction with the other two types. The findings offer valuable insights into enhancing the efficiency of InGaP/GaAs solar cells.

articleTitle: Implementation of “Emad-Falih Transform” to Resolve Electrical Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: In view of the importance of finding solutions to the problems of electrical circuits and proving the ability of integrative transformations to find solutions to these issues, in this paper, using the Emad-Falih transform which converts the most difficult differential equations into simple algebraic equations and proves the ability of this transform to solve many problems of general electrical circuits easily With accurate results. It is worth noting that each integral transformation is not better than the other. Each integral transformation solves a specific real-life problem.

articleTitle: Optimization of COCOMO-II Model Parameters Using Hybrid Algorithm of Cuckoo Search Algorithm and GA
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a classification model for the detection of phishing domains based on classification rules. We formulate these rules based on the results of the analysis and distribute them into three classifiers: the first is related to domain name features, the second is related to SEO information of the domain, and the third is related to security scans by security vendors. Each classifier feds its results to the main classifier, which then evaluates the received results by its rule. We formulate eleven classification rules, which are distributed as follows: six rules for the first classifier, four rules for the second classifier, and one rule for the third classifier. We retrieved domain names from 222 confirmed phishing URLs, tested them using the suggested model, and obtained a 99.1% accuracy rate.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis and Comparison Between Fuzzy Logic Algorithm and PI-Controller in Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Technologies based on renewable energy are maturing into viable choices for providing quick, dependable power to every home in the world. Since solar radiation, cell temperatures, and environmental conditions all fluctuate, the output power from solar photovoltaic modules is unpredictable. Therefore, maximum power point trackers are required to maximize solar energy collection and enhance photovoltaic system performance. In this article, we'll deal with two MPPT controllers that are different from each other in approach, Performance in tracking toward fast irradiance and temperature change is examined between a proportional-integral (PI) controller and a fuzzy logic controller by MATLAB/Simulink. Based on the simulation results, it was clear that the fuzzy logic controller outperformed the PI controller. The fuzzy logic controller can dampen oscillation while also providing a fast reaction to fluctuations in solar radiation, and unlike the conventional PI controller, it doesn't even need the settings adjusted.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Chronic Kidney Disease Progression Using Longitudinal Clinical Data and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a prevalent condition with significant morbidity and mortality. Early and accurate detection is critical for effective treatment and management. This paper presents a comparative analysis of deep learning techniques, specifically Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP) models, for predicting CKD. We preprocessed a dataset containing clinical and demographic features, trained MLP models of varying complexities, and evaluated their performances. The results showed that simpler models achieved high accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores, comparable to more complex models. These findings suggest that deep learning can be a valuable tool in the early detection of CKD, with the potential to support clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: Horizontal Slot Waveguide for High-Performance Optical Modulator
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Vanadium dioxide (VO2) is the most widely used phase change material for realizing electro-absorption modulators. VO2 undergoes a rapid phase transition from insulation to metallic phase when stimulated by an electric field larger than its threshold transition field. In this study, a three-layer slot waveguide modulator featuring a VO2 active layer for TM mode operation at a wavelength of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda=1.55\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> is designed. The proposed modulator employs ultra-thin silicon ion implant layers instead of metal contacts, resulting in a substantial improvement in modulator performance. Simulation results based on finite-difference time-domain (FDTD), reveal a high extinction ratio of about −10 dB.

articleTitle: Implementing V/F Control of Three-Phase Induction Motors without the Use of Digital Processors for Electric Propulsion Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: A V/F control method is implemented in this paper without digital processors and only with electronic circuits. Three-phase induction motors are typically controlled using the V IF control method. Digital processors are sometimes viewed as a source of concern in some applications, such as ships, where security and reliability are of great importance. Several concerns have been raised concerning the potential for hang-ups due to poor environmental conditions, such as temperature and humidity, as well as the impact of a noise-free environment and the possibility of hacking. Accordingly, if electronic circuits for this equipment can be implemented without digital processors, the level of security and reliability in this sector will be dramatically enhanced. Specifically, the control unit of propulsion systems is the part of ships studied in this paper. Controlling the ship's engine speed and ensuring a safe start-up is the primary goal of this section. A digital processor is not used in this paper to achieve this goal. Through the PSIM software, simulations and results can be viewed. A simulation of the proposed circuit confirms its feasibility.

articleTitle: Development of an Ultra-Sensitive Magnetic-Based Biosensor; a Simulation Study
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: This study presents an advanced magnetic biosensor design incorporating an L-shaped ferromagnetic core with UL dimensions and an air gap replaced by highly porous aluminum or copper foam later-filled biological samples containing high-permeability ferromagnetic nanoparticles. The sensor detects specific biological molecules through magnetic field interactions. The system's electrical parameters were methodically optimized for enhanced performance. The research investigated the impact of various materials on the air gap's magnetic properties and assessed the relationships between permeability, output-induced voltage, input voltage, and input frequency. Findings indicate that using materials with higher magnetic permeability, such as Magnetite (Fe304) or Cobalt ferrite (CoFe2O4) ferrofluids, considerably improved the biosensor's performance by optimizing magnetic coupling between primary and secondary windings. This innovative magnetic biosensor holds potential for diverse applications, including medical diagnostics, environmental monitoring, and industrial process control. The study offers valuable insights into magnetic biosensor design and optimization, facilitating heightened sensitivity and selectivity in detecting target molecules.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Distance Technique to Optimize the K-Nearest Neighbor Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Engineering Conference on Electrical, Energy, and Artificial Intelligence (EICEEAI)
abstract: Plenty of Bayesian-consistent, heuristic and statistical classifiers have been introduced. Although support vector machines, deep neural networks, and random forests exhibit acceptable performance in several fields, their primary challenge lies in the lengthy training phase, especially when dealing with big data. K-nearest neighbors (KNN) is one of the simplest, Bayesian consistent and most common algorithms for classification tasks which locally makes its decision and there is no need to any training phase, can be implemented by parallel processing algorithms which makes it suitable to deal with big datasets.
